identification.name: Silicon Carbide (Sintered)
identification.common_form_notes: Supplied as sintered near-net-shape billets, tiles, or finished components. Machining requires diamond or CBN (cubic boron nitride) tooling; conventional cutting destroys the tooling. Final grinding/lapping to tight tolerances is standard for precision optical and bearing applications.
identification.notes: Pressureless-sintered silicon carbide (SSiC / SC-30 grade, >98% theoretical density). SiC does not have a conventional melting point — it decomposes by sublimation above approximately 2730 °C. Maximum service temperature in air is limited to ~1375 °C by oxidation; in inert or vacuum environments, service to ~1650 °C is possible. Tensile strength is highly flaw-limited and variable; apply appropriate Weibull statistics and safety factors (do not use mean strength for design without a Weibull modulus). CTE (coefficient of thermal expansion) is approximately constant from 0–600 °C at ~4 µm/m·K. Electrical conductivity is effectively zero for structural sintered grades (impurity-doped SiC can be semiconducting but is not the structural form).

typical_usage: Precision bearings, seals, and pump components in corrosive or high-temperature media; semiconductor process equipment (wafer carriers, susceptors); thermal management substrates; ballistic armor tiles; high-temperature heat exchangers; mirror substrates and precision optical structures where maximum specific stiffness and dimensional stability at temperature are required.
